screen: S02 actual root playable battle screen

failureBeingRepaired.summary: The technically integrated root screen is materially below the binding completed-screen baseline in battle density, four-member party identity, attack/reward causality, layer hierarchy and mobile commercial finish.

visualAuthority.primary: The user-defined completed S02 battle-screen image supplied in the project conversation, interpreted as structural direction rather than copyable art or exact UI.
bindingTraits: battle is the dominant scene within five seconds
a persistent four-slot party identity is visible
enemy threat and current objective are immediately legible
contact, attack, hit, defeat and reward form an understandable visual chain
warm wood and brass Cat's Tower chrome frames the scene without crushing it
commerce remains a support layer below the battle rather than the screen's protagonist
five-tab navigation remains stable and thumb reachable
copyingForbidden: competitor names, probabilities, prices or game values
flattened generated full-screen art used as the interface

truthfulnessContract.actualProgress: game.floor, game.kills, game.killNeed and guardian HP
truthfulnessContract.actualCausality: actual attack timers plus non-consuming observation of game.emit events
truthfulnessContract.fourSlotIdentity: first four canonical visible job slots with explicit owned, on-field, available or locked labels
prohibited: showing an unowned member as an active field unit
minting or modifying coins, ruby, rewards, ownership, levels or unlocks
changing game-core.js, game-data.js, app.js or sealed simulation contracts
using a second persistent state store

requiredVisualRepair: replace the sparse center field with a staged combat corridor, foreground depth, readable enemy threat and active contact lane
keep actual cats and enemies large enough to identify on 320px width
show four persistent party slots and the real status of each slot
show a visible encounter objective and progress meter derived from actual state
show actual hit, faint, kill and reward feedback without consuming or duplicating game events
show an actual contact and next-attack explanation so the player understands why damage occurs
keep summon as the playable core's explicit temporary reinforcement command and do not mislabel it as a canonical active skill
reduce event-banner and shortcut dominance so they no longer displace the battle
repair 320px resource values, labels and lower information hierarchy
retain actual agency, forge, item, shop, return and commerce navigation behavior

rules: no document or body horizontal overflow
battle scene height is at least 320 CSS pixels
four party slots remain present and distinguishable
critical interactive controls remain at least 44 CSS pixels
bottom navigation remains pinned and reachable
large-text simulation introduces no horizontal overflow

browserAcceptance: root runtime bridge and renderer report ready
renderer reports partySlotCount 4 and visualCausalityReady true
normal screenshots are captured only after real summon button interactions create a readable active battle; the report records this interaction
agency opens the actual existing sheet
commerce moves to the actual merchant section
unavailable events expose an explicit pending state
console and uncaught page errors equal zero
visualCriticQuestions: Can a new player identify the cats, enemy, floor, current objective and next action within five seconds?
Does the screen read as a Cat's Tower battle rather than a generic dashboard or sparse prototype?
Are the four party slots honest about active, owned and locked state?
Can the player follow contact to attack to damage to defeat to reward?
At 320px, are resource values and primary actions readable without zoom?
Does commerce remain visibly subordinate to battle?
automaticFailConditions: game-core, game-data, app, save schema or economy values changed
unowned members shown as active field combatants
fake skill or reward state presented as functional
actual event queue consumed or duplicated
horizontal overflow at a required viewport
